body: Super Mario Strikers is Next Level Games' GameCube football game, putting Mario characters into fast five-a-side matches surrounded by electric barriers. A captain, three sidekicks and a goalkeeper form each team. Passing, shooting and tackling establish the sport's familiar purpose, while items and exaggerated physical contact turn its routes into opportunities for interference. The ball stays in play inside the arena, keeping the contest moving. The player has to create an opening while expecting the other team to use something much less sporting than an ordinary defensive challenge.

Only the captain can perform a Super Strike, a charged attempt worth two goals when successfully timed and scored. Preparing it requires enough space to complete the action without interruption. Shells, bananas and other items can disable opponents, giving the attacking team a brief opportunity to move or shoot. Ordinary passes remain important because they can create a faster opening than a prolonged special move. The player continually weighs the reliable immediate attempt against the greater reward attached to a shot that leaves its striker exposed for longer.

Next Level Games brought experience from NHL Hitz Pro to the game's forceful tackles and rapid changes of possession. Bowser can enter the arena to disrupt both sides, giving the match another temporary problem. Released first in Europe as Mario Smash Football in 2005, it became the beginning of a separate Mario sports series. The original's clarity comes from keeping the destination simple. The ball still has to cross the goal line, but almost everything between recovering possession and taking the shot can become a comic act of sabotage.
